key_insight: DeHNSSo-v2 extends harmonic Navier–Stokes analysis to compressible flows over curved geometries while delivering approximately 10× speed-ups on DeHNSSo-v1 nonlinear test cases.
engineering_relevance: The open-source solver supports boundary-layer transition and flow-control studies involving nonlinear disturbances, complex surfaces, and metamaterials across compressibility regimes.
method: Compressible formulation on body-fitted 2D grids with automatic mesh generation and fourth-order spatial accuracy.
Linear-cost sparse assembly and reusable per-mode factorizations reduce computational cost.
Newton pseudo-arclength continuation tracks high-amplitude nonlinear solutions.
evidence_signal: Validation covers linear boundary-layer instability at Mach 0.5–4.5, nonlinear oblique-mode breakdown at Mach 1.6, swept-wing crossflow against DNS, and resonator–wave interaction against experimentally validated simulations.
watch_item: The reported speed-up is specific to DeHNSSo-v1 nonlinear benchmarks; performance on new geometries and harmonic resolutions requires verification.
paper_title: DeHNSSo-v2: A compressible, curvilinear, and efficient extension of the Delft Harmonic Navier-Stokes Solver
